merger_description:
Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation (**CSC**), as trustee of the ARIA Property Fund (**APF**), proposes to acquire 50% of the units in each of the Watergardens Trust (**Asset Trust**) and the Watergardens Trading Trust (**Trading Trust**), from QIC Retail Pty Ltd, as trustee of the QIC Town Centre Fund, and QTCF TT Midco Pty Ltd, respectively (the **Acquisition**).

The remaining 50% of the units in the Asset Trust and Trading Trust will be retained by the existing unitholders following the Acquisition, being QIC Retail (No. 2) Pty Ltd, as trustee for QIC Retail (No. 2) Fund, and QPF TT Midco Pty Ltd, respectively.

The Asset Trust owns the freehold land at 399 Melton Hwy, Taylors Lake, Vic 3038, comprising the Watergardens Shopping Centre precinct located in Melbourne’s outer north-west. The Watergardens Shopping Centre precinct is centred around the Watergardens Shopping Centre. Watergardens Shopping Centre’s tenant mix includes discount department stores, supermarkets, furniture stores and approximately 175 speciality retailers. The Watergardens Shopping Centre precinct also includes office space, an 86-room hotel, and various pad sites (e.g., a Dan Murphy’s and United Petroleum service station).

The Asset Trust holds the property for the primary purpose of leasing retail and commercial space within the precinct to tenants, including the shopping centre’s retailers, the office tenants, Quest Apartment Hotels and pad site operators. The Trading Trust does not have any assets or business activities at present but was established to carry out investment activities related to the Watergardens Shopping Centre. The units of the Asset Trust and Trading Trust are stapled to each other.

Through the Acquisition, CSC, as the trustee of the APF, will acquire an indirect 50% interest in the Watergardens Shopping Centre precinct.

CSC is a corporate Commonwealth entity, established under Commonwealth legislation, which provides superannuation schemes for Australian Government employees and Australian Defence Force members. The APF is wholly owned by CSC’s pooled superannuation trust, ARIA Investments Trust. CSC is the trustee of the APF. GPT Group (**GPT**), an Australian real estate investment manager, acts as investment manager of the APF on behalf of CSC.

Affiliates of QIC Limited, an Australian investment manager, provide property management, development management and leasing management services in relation to the Watergardens Shopping Centre and will continue to do so following the Acquisition.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between CSC and GPT,
and the Watergardens Shopping Centre, in the supply of
retail space to retailers and the supply of shopping centre
amenities to shoppers in the north-west metropolitan
Melbourne area
b. there are alternative shopping and retail centres in north-
west metropolitan Melbourne.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
